## Linked issue or supporting maintainer

<!-- Keep the one line that applies and delete the others. Link an issue labeled "actionable", or name the maintainer who agreed to this change beforehand. PRs with neither will be automatically closed, unless the author has write access to the repo. -->

Fixes #199121 <!-- Issue number -->

## BC-breaking?

<!-- If this change breaks backward compatibility, describe the impact and migration path. Otherwise, write "No". -->
The engine list on aarch64 is now only onednn and qnnpack, from qnnpack, onednn, x86, and fbgemm.

## Summary (human written only)

Reland of the already-reverted 199121 with a change that now oneDNN uses fbgemm path for FP16.


## Agent details (if applicable)

### What this changes

- `at::Context::supportedQEngines()` / `qEngine()`: on AArch64, `x86` and `fbgemm` are no longer
  registered even when PyTorch is built with `USE_FBGEMM`. FBGEMM's quantized int8 kernels do
  not run on AArch64 (#177254: the X86 default engine crashed in FBGEMM with "unknown
  architecture"). `fbgemmSupportedCPU()` is no longer what decides AArch64 engine registration.
- The dense int8 linear/conv prepack, conv unpack, conv deserialization, and
  `LinearPackedParams.__setstate__` paths compile out the X86/FBGEMM arms on AArch64, so the ONEDNN
  arm is the only AArch64 path. These guards and engine registration in `Context.cpp` use the same
  predicate: `defined(USE_FBGEMM) && !defined(__aarch64__) && !defined(_M_ARM64)`. The sparse
  (`ao_sparse`) FBGEMM arms are untouched; they are unreachable on AArch64 because the FBGEMM
  engine can no longer be selected there.
- fp16 dynamic linear (the reason for the revert): FBGEMM's fp16 kernels do work on AArch64,
  and oneDNN has no fp16 `LinearPackedParams`. On AArch64, under the ONEDNN engine,
  `quantized::linear_prepack_fp16` and `LinearPackedParams.__setstate__` (TorchScript/pickle
  load of fp16 packed params) now build `PackedLinearWeightFp16`.

### Why fp16-under-ONEDNN routing is AArch64-only

On AArch64, ONEDNN is the default engine and X86/FBGEMM cannot be selected. Without the
routing, FBGEMM's fp16 linear would be unreachable. On x86, fp16 linear is already reachable
through X86/FBGEMM. Those engines are only registered when `fbgemmSupportedCPU()` is true. A
user can select ONEDNN explicitly on a CPU where FBGEMM's kernels can't run, so routing ONEDNN
to FBGEMM there could crash instead of raising. x86 behavior is therefore unchanged: ONEDNN
still raises for fp16 prepack.

### BC-breaking (AArch64 only)

All of the following apply only to AArch64 builds with `USE_FBGEMM` (the default). x86 is
unaffected.

- `torch.backends.quantized.supported_engines` no longer lists `"x86"` or `"fbgemm"`. It is
  typically `['qnnpack', 'onednn']`.
- The default `torch.backends.quantized.engine` changes from `"x86"` to `"onednn"`.
- `torch.backends.quantized.engine = "x86"` (or `"fbgemm"`) now raises
  `RuntimeError: quantized engine X86 is not supported`. Code that sets the engine
  unconditionally should pick from `supported_engines`, e.g.
  `"x86" if "x86" in torch.backends.quantized.supported_engines else "onednn"`.
- Knock-on effects of the engine change:
  - FX convert decides `reduce_range` from the engine (`torch/ao/quantization/fx/convert.py`),
    so it is now `False` (ONEDNN) instead of `True` (X86).
  - Engine-keyed helpers such as `get_default_qconfig(torch.backends.quantized.engine)` /
    `get_default_qconfig_mapping(...)` now return the `onednn` configs. `get_default_qconfig("x86")`
    still returns an x86 qconfig, but the resulting model can't run on an x86 engine.
- int8 linear/conv prepack now always goes through oneDNN (`PackedLinearWeightsOnednn` /
  `PackedConvWeightsOnednn`). oneDNN requires a weight `zero_point` of 0 (symmetric weights).
  Asymmetric int8 weights that FBGEMM used to accept now raise at prepack. Use symmetric weight
  observers, such as the ones the default `onednn` qconfigs use.
- Serialized quantized models whose packed params were saved on AArch64 under X86/FBGEMM load
  under the current engine, which is ONEDNN by default. The asymmetric-weight restriction above
  also applies on load.
- fp16 dynamic linear (`quantized::linear_prepack_fp16`, `nn.quantized.dynamic.Linear` with
  `dtype=torch.float16`, fp16 dynamic LSTM/GRU) on AArch64 now requires a oneDNN-enabled build
  (`USE_MKLDNN=ON`, the default). With `USE_FBGEMM=ON` and `USE_MKLDNN=OFF`, the only registered
  engine is `qnnpack` and the default engine is `none`. fp16 prepack then raises (it is not
  supported by QNNPACK, and there is no engine for it under `none`); before this change it worked
  through the X86 engine. This change does not route fp16 under QNNPACK/`none` to FBGEMM. QNNPACK's
  "not supported" contract is shared with mobile builds, and `none` means no quantized engine is
  available, so routing either one would add a second per-arch special case for a non-default
  build configuration.

### Tests

- `TestDynamicQuantizedOps.test_qlinear_dynamic_fp16_serialization` (new): prepacks fp16 linear
  params under a pinned engine (`onednn` on AArch64, `fbgemm` elsewhere), checks unpack,
  TorchScript script+save+load (exercises the C++ `__setstate__`), and compares against
  `F.linear` with fp16-rounded weights.
- `skipIfNoFBGEMMFp16Linear` (new, `common_quantization.py`): checks the same thing as
  `skipIfNoFBGEMM` when `fbgemm` is registered (x86 unchanged). It also accepts AArch64 builds
  with FBGEMM compiled in and ONEDNN available. These tests use it, so they run on AArch64 again:
  - the existing fp16 FBGEMM tests in `TestDynamicQuantizedOps`,
  - `TestQuantizeJit.test_linear_dynamic_fp16`,
  - the `TestQuantizeEagerPTQDynamic` class (int8 and fp16 dynamic Linear/LSTM/RNNCell,
    scripting, and serialization under the default ONEDNN engine; its two embedding tests keep
    `@skipIfNoFBGEMM`).
- Coverage drop on AArch64: the remaining 224 `@skipIfNoFBGEMM` sites (tests or classes) skip on
  AArch64 now that `fbgemm` is not in `supported_engines`. Most are in
  `test/quantization/fx/` (`test_numeric_suite_fx.py`, `test_quantize_fx.py`,
  `test_model_report_fx.py`, `test_equalize_fx.py`) and `test/quantization/jit/`, with smaller
  numbers in `core/` and `eager/`. Before this change they ran on AArch64 under the X86/FBGEMM
  engine or the default engine. Some do not need the fbgemm engine (for example quantized
  embedding / embedding_bag, which run under ONEDNN on AArch64). Moving them to an
  engine-appropriate guard is left as a follow-up.
- `TestQuantizedConv.test_qconv1d_module_supported_engines` (#177254 regression): runs
  quantized `Conv1d` under every supported engine and compares against a
  dequantize -> `F.conv1d` -> quantize reference.
- `TestTorch.test_qengine_aarch64` (new, next to `test_qengine`): on AArch64, x86/fbgemm are
  neither listed nor settable, and a fresh process's default engine is `onednn` when oneDNN is
  available.
- Docstring for `torch.ao.nn.quantized.ConvTranspose3d` no longer sets
  `engine = 'fbgemm'` (raises on AArch64) or claims only FBGEMM is implemented. ONEDNN and
  QNNPACK also run it.

cc @jgong5 @mingfeima @XiaobingSuper @sanchitintel @ashokei @jingxu10 @aditew01
title: Stop registering X86/FBGEMM quantized engines on AArch64
